report:
## Conclusion: FALSE — Drinking boiled garlic water does **not** cure COVID-19.

This claim emerged early in the pandemic and has been repeatedly debunked by health authorities and fact-checkers. The World Health Organization states there is currently no licensed medication to cure COVID-19 and has explicitly addressed garlic-related misinformation as a myth. AFP Fact Check reported as early as February 2020 that health professionals found no evidence supporting garlic as an effective COVID-19 treatment. FactCheck.org similarly published an article titled "Garlic Isn't a Cure," classifying boiled garlic among fake coronavirus cures circulating online.

While garlic does contain compounds (such as allicin) that show some antimicrobial and antiviral activity in laboratory studies, there is no scientific evidence that consuming garlic — boiled or otherwise — prevents or treats COVID-19. General health benefits of garlic are not a substitute for targeted antiviral therapies or vaccines. Health authorities including the WHO and CDC advise against using garlic as a COVID-19 treatment.

**Sources:**
- https://factcheck.afp.com/theres-no-scientific-proof-tonic-onions-ginger-garlic-and-lemon-can-cure-covid-19
- https://www.who.int/emergencies/diseases/novel-coronavirus-2019/advice-for-public/myth-busters
- https://www.factcheck.org/2020/02/fake-coronavirus-cures-part-2-garlic-isnt-a-cure/
- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32836826/
